title: Jam Roly-Poly
subtitle: Suet pastry rolled with jam and steamed or baked
excerpt: A classic British school-dinner pudding: suet pastry spread with jam, rolled up, and either steamed in a cloth or baked in the oven until the pastry is soft and yielding and the jam bleeds through. Serve with hot custard.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jam roly-poly is documented in British recipe collections from the mid-nineteenth century under various names including the Dead Man's Arm (from the shape of a steamed roll wrapped in a cloth) and Dead Man's Leg. The dish became a staple of school dinners and institutional cooking in the twentieth century, served with yellow custard in a pattern so consistent that the combination is now a shorthand for the peculiarities of British state catering. The suet pastry used for the roll is the same as for steamed puddings: shredded suet mixed with self-raising flour and water, which produces a tender, slightly fatty texture quite unlike shortcrust. Strawberry or raspberry jam is traditional, though any jam works.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin lined with baking paper for the oven method.

content.text: Leave a 2 cm border of bare pastry around the edge when spreading the jam so it does not leak out of the ends when rolled. Seal the roll firmly and place it seam-side down. For the oven method, wrap the roll loosely in foil (the steam inside the foil is what makes it soft) and bake at 190 C for 35 to 40 minutes.

Mix the flour, suet, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add about 100 ml of cold water, a little at a time, until a soft but not sticky dough forms. Turn onto a floured surface and roll into a rectangle roughly 23 by 30 cm.

Spread the jam over the pastry, leaving a 2 cm border around all the edges. Roll up from one of the short ends into a log, pinching the seam and ends to seal. Place seam-side down on a large sheet of baking paper.

Wrap loosely in the baking paper, then wrap again in foil, pleating the top to allow for expansion. Bake in a preheated oven at 190 C (170 C fan) for 35 to 40 minutes. Unwrap carefully and serve in slices with hot custard.
